title: U.S. Department of Energy Allocates $159 Million in Phase II Genesis Mission Awards for Quantum Error Correction and Materials Co-Design - Quantum Computing Report
gist: DOE announced 12 Phase II Genesis Mission awards totaling $159M, capping 297 projects; quantum-relevant projects include Harvard's AI-driven QEC co-design (ASQC), ORNL's AI inverse design of quantum magnets, Fermilab's AXESS cryogenic chip-design workflow, and LBNL's Osprey agentic AI for accelerators. The common thread is using AI to compress quantum hardware, materials and chip design cycles.

insights.claim: DOE announced 12 Phase II Genesis Mission awards totaling $159 million, capping an initial cohort of 297 projects.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Federal AI-for-science spending is flowing at scale and touching quantum supply chains.

insights.claim: Of the 12 Phase II projects, two specifically target quantum hardware scaling, QEC co-design and quantum materials synthesis.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum is a minority share of Genesis money; most goes to broader AI/HPC science.

themes.theme: AI as accelerator for quantum engineering

insights.claim: Harvard's ASQC project uses AI optimization with physical quantum processors to automate QEC code selection and reduce error-correction overhead for scientific workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lower QEC overhead directly reduces the qubit count needed for useful FTQC, pulling timelines forward.

insights.claim: ORNL leads a physics-informed AI framework that works backward from target properties to design quantum magnetic materials for sensing, low-power microelectronics and QPU hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Inverse materials design may unlock new qubit and sensor materials.

insights.claim: Fermilab's AXESS project, with AMD, IBM and SLAC, applies AI to compress custom chip design cycles from months to minutes for radiation-hardened and sub-Kelvin cryogenic ICs needed by FTQC testbeds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cryo-CMOS control electronics are a scaling chokepoint; faster design cycles benefit chip partners.
insights.quote: apply AI models that compress chip design cycles from months to minutes
insights.locator: A key focus across the awards

insights.claim: Fermilab's Phase I QCVV project with NVIDIA, IBM, Purdue, Quantum Machines and University of Chicago uses closed-loop AI agents to choose optimal quantum state measurements, cutting data acquisition overhead.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-driven characterization reduces the cost of quantum device calibration.
insights.locator: A key focus across the awards

insights.claim: LBNL's MOAT-Core expands its agentic AI assistant Osprey across 16 institutions and eight national labs to automate accelerator operations, including beamlines and EUV lithography tools used for microelectronics and quantum components.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Agentic AI is being deployed in real physical infrastructure operations, not just software.

insights.claim: The OSTP Genesis framework includes AI-driven quantum algorithm discovery that automates circuit compilation without domain-specific knowledge, plus real-time AI agents for noise mitigation, adaptive QEC decoding and quantum sensing network control.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-quantum convergence is official US policy, supporting GPU/AI vendors in the quantum stack.
